instruments_run.reason: ensurepip SIGABRT building resolver venv under uv cpython-3.13
Go binary, not installable via uvx/PyPI

audit.trust_model: Operator runs CLI locally (trusted). UNTRUSTED surface = the 57 target repos' code executed/tested inside Docker + LLM-generated patches + remote git/AWS-Bedrock/GitHub API responses (incl. test-runner XML).
audit.coverage_note: Static + instrumented sweep of source roots commit0/ (70), agent/ (38), tools/ (47). Excluded from source counts: commit0/data/test_ids/*.bz2 (1067 fixtures), vendored stub samples. Coverage % NOT measured (no test execution; would require Docker + secrets).

findings.title: Duplicate test-class names silently shadow earlier classes (lost coverage)
findings.why: In a single module Python binds the last class definition only. The earlier same-named test class is overwritten before pytest collects it, so those assertions NEVER execute. The suite reports green while silently skipping real tests — false confidence in a benchmark whose entire value is test correctness.
findings.remediation: Rename the duplicate classes (e.g. TestPathConstants -> TestPathConstantsExtended) or merge their methods. Add ruff F811 as a merge-blocking CI gate so this cannot recur.

findings.title: XML parsed without defusedxml on untrusted test-runner output (XXE/billion-laughs)
findings.why: These parsers consume JUnit/test XML produced by executing the 57 untrusted target repos' test suites. A malicious target repo could emit a crafted XML with an external DTD (XXE) or entity-expansion bomb. Exploitability is bounded: stdlib ElementTree resolves no external entities by default on modern CPython, hence Medium/HOLD rather than High — but the harness's threat model explicitly treats target-repo output as attacker-controlled.
findings.remediation: Replace `xml.etree.ElementTree` with `defusedxml.ElementTree` in the 4 parse sites (single root-cause fix). Add defusedxml to dependencies.

findings.title: urllib.urlopen with unvalidated scheme (file:// / SSRF surface)
findings.why: urlopen called on URLs not pinned to http(s); a file:// or other scheme could read local files if the URL is influenced by repo metadata. Privilege required is high (operator-controlled config in most paths), so Medium/HOLD.
findings.remediation: Validate scheme in {http, https} before urlopen, or use requests with an explicit allowlist. One helper closes all 4 sites.

findings.title: Core deps pinned to moving git branches (non-reproducible builds)
findings.why: Two core runtime dependencies resolve from `branch = "main"` on third-party (Ethara-Ai) forks. Although uv.lock pins a commit today, any lock refresh re-resolves the branch HEAD, so two installs days apart can ship different code. Supply-chain risk: the fork owner can alter behaviour without a version bump. Reproducibility is foundational for a benchmark whose results must be comparable across time.
findings.remediation: Pin to an immutable rev (tag or commit SHA: aider-chat = {git=..., rev=<sha>}). Document the fork divergence rationale. Keep uv.lock authoritative in CI (uv sync --frozen).

findings.title: Dependency CVE scan could not be performed (assessment limitation)
findings.why: ASSESSMENT LIMITATION, not a product defect. No CVE scanner could run in this sandbox, so known-vulnerability status of the dependency tree is UNKNOWN. This lowers confidence on the Dependencies axis; it is not itself evidence of a vulnerability.
findings.remediation: Run pip-audit/osv-scanner in CI on a clean runner (the crash here is environment-specific to uv-managed cpython-3.13 ensurepip). Add as a merge-blocking job.

findings.title: Compiled binary committed to git (tools/gostubber/gostubber, 3.99 MB Mach-O)
evidence: CMD:git verify-pack/rev-list CMD-016 (tools/gostubber/gostubber = 3.99MB, Mach-O arm64 executable)
findings.why: A platform-specific compiled binary is tracked in source control. It bloats .git permanently, is non-portable (arm64 Mach-O only), and is a supply-chain/trust hazard (binary blobs are unreviewable in PRs). Go source (go.mod) is present, so the binary is a build artifact that should not be versioned.
findings.remediation: git rm --cached the binary, add to .gitignore, build from tools/gostubber source in CI/setup. Consider git-filter-repo to purge history if .git size matters.

findings.title: 23 MB animated GIF + .docx committed (repo bloat, .git = 161 MB)
findings.why: A 23.3 MB GIF dominates clone time and .git size forever. Binary office docs (.docx) don't diff and bloat history. For a benchmark people clone repeatedly, this is real friction.
findings.remediation: Move large media to Git LFS or external hosting (link from README). Convert the GIF to a hosted MP4/webm. Remove .docx in favour of markdown. Enable pre-commit check-added-large-files with a strict cap (it is already configured but evidently the gif predates it).

findings.title: 9,612 residual lint violations + broadly suppressed pyright type-checking
findings.why: The bulk are style/docstring/annotation gaps (low risk), but the volume means real signals (201 unused imports, 68 unused vars) are buried, and pyright is dialed down so type regressions pass silently. For a long-lived multi-language harness this erodes maintainability.
findings.remediation: Burn down F401/F841 (auto-fixable). Incrementally re-enable pyright strictness per-module. Make ruff check (current selection) merge-blocking so the count cannot grow.

findings.title: Redundant re-imports and non-PEP8 import alias (NITs)
findings.why: Cosmetic only. The F821 is a FALSE-POSITIVE-for-runtime: line 111 is a quoted type annotation ('docker.DockerClient') that Python never evaluates; docker is lazily imported at line 91. No NameError occurs.
findings.remediation: Remove the in-function re-imports; alias TestStatus with CamelCase; move the docker type-only import under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` to satisfy the linter.

findings.title: No coverage floor enforced + ruff version skew between pre-commit and pyproject
evidence: ABSENCE:no --cov/coverage config in pyproject.toml (CMD-069 grep cov => empty)
SRC:.pre-commit-config.yaml ruff rev v0.6.1 vs pyproject requires ruff>=0.6.4 (CMD-022)
findings.why: 116 test files exist (good), but CI enforces no coverage minimum, so coverage can silently regress. The pre-commit ruff (v0.6.1) lags the project's required ruff (>=0.6.4), so contributors and CI may lint with different rule behaviour.
findings.remediation: Add pytest-cov with a coverage floor in CI. Bump pre-commit ruff rev to match pyproject (>=0.6.4) to eliminate drift.

findings.title: Secret handling is clean (no hardcoded creds, no secrets in history)
evidence: CMD:git-history secret scan CMD-041 (no BEGIN PRIVATE/AKIA/sk-/ghp_/bearer matches across full history of .env/*.pem/*.key)
findings.why: Genuine positive. Credentials come exclusively from env vars; only .env.example is tracked; no secret ever appears in git history. This is the correct pattern.
findings.remediation: None. Maintain via a CI secret-scanning gate (gitleaks/trufflehog) to keep it clean.

findings.title: Tar extraction is path-traversal guarded (bandit B202 is a false positive)
evidence: SRC:commit0/harness/docker_utils.py:100-129 (safe_extract + is_within_directory guard raising 'Attempted Path Traversal in Tar File' before extractall)
findings.why: Disclosed false positive. bandit flags tarfile.extractall as HIGH but the code wraps it in safe_extract() which validates every member stays within the target dir before extraction. The other 2 bandit-HIGH (MD5 in agents_java.py:268, scrape_pdf.py:303) are also FPs: MD5 used only for short filename hashing, not security.
findings.remediation: Optionally pass usedforsecurity=False to the MD5 calls to silence the scanner. No functional change needed.

findings.title: MIT license present and consistent
findings.why: Genuine positive. Clear permissive license at root and in metadata.
